## STANDING HEXAGRAM STRUCTURE

- 錯卦 Inverse Hexagram: #63 既濟 / LXIII. The Kî Žî Hexagram
- 綜卦 Reversed Hexagram: #63 既濟 / LXIII. The Kî Žî Hexagram

### 卦辭

#### 武英殿本

未濟：亨，小狐汔濟，濡其尾，无攸利。

#### Legge

Wei Žî intimates progress and success (in the circumstances which it implies). (We see) a young fox that has nearly crossed (the stream), when its tail gets immersed. There will be no advantage in any way.

### 大象

#### 武英殿本

火在水上，未濟；君子以慎辨物居方。

#### Legge

LXIV. (The trigram representing) water and that for fire above it form Wei Žî. The superior man, in accordance with this, carefully discriminates among (the qualities of) things, and the (different) positions they (naturally) occupy.

### 初六

#### 武英殿本

初六：濡其尾，吝。

#### Legge

1. The first SIX, divided, shows its subject (like a fox) whose tail gets immersed. There will be occasion for regret.

### 小象

#### 武英殿本

濡其尾，亦不知極也。

#### Legge

1. 'His tail gets immersed:'--this is the very height of ignorance.

## EMERGING HEXAGRAM STRUCTURE

- 錯卦 Inverse Hexagram: #39 蹇 / XXXIX. The Kien Hexagram

### 卦辭

#### 武英殿本

睽：小事吉。

#### Legge

Khwei indicates that, (notwithstanding the condition of things which it denotes), in small matters there will (still) be good success.

### 大象

#### 武英殿本

上火下澤，睽；君子以同而異。

#### Legge

XXXVIII. (The trigram representing) fire above, and that for (the waters of) a marsh below, form Khwei. The superior man, in accordance with this, where there is a general agreement, yet admits diversity.
